# Submission

- One PDF per team to Canvas, rendered from a Quarto document in your team's GitHub repo.
- A URL to your 5–7 minute team video presentation.
- Final commit pushed to GitHub repo by the deadline.

**Due:** Friday, June 26, 11:59 p.m.

::: callout-important
## Hard requirements

Your report must meet all of these. Missing any one costs the associated rubric points (and a missing required section can cost more than its line item, since dependent items also fail).

- **Structure:** all sections in the [Required report structure](index.qmd#required-report-structure), in order.
- **Length:** at least **10 pages of body** (narrative + figures + tables). The title page, references, and Code Appendix do **not** count.
- **Figures:** at least **three**, each with a caption, a numbered cross-reference, and discussion in the text.
- **Table:** at least **one** non-trivial (summary/aggregated) table, captioned and cross-referenced.
- **Multivariate figure:** at least **one** figure showing **3+ variables**.
- **Code:** in the Code Appendix only.
:::

# Rubric (100 points)

Components below follow the required report structure in the [project guidelines](index.qmd#required-report-structure). Each figure earns its points only when it has a caption, is cross-referenced by number from the narrative, and is discussed in the text.

| Component | Points |
|---|---|
| Introduction & Motivation — clear and engaging | 4 |
| Research question(s) explicitly stated | 4 |
| Data Provenance documented (source, collector, purpose, cases) | 5 |
| Variables described and justified | 4 |
| Data Wrangling & Cleaning explained in narrative (not just code) | 5 |
| Non-trivial summary table (caption + cross-reference + discussion) | 5 |
| Figure 1 (caption + cross-reference + discussion) | 4 |
| Figure 2 (caption + cross-reference + discussion) | 4 |
| Figure 3 (caption + cross-reference + discussion) | 4 |
| At least one figure displays 3+ variables effectively | 4 |
| Findings / Conclusions clearly stated and tied to question(s) | 6 |
| Limitations & Future Work discussion | 4 |
| Body meets the 10-page minimum (narrative only; appendix/refs excluded) | 3 |
| References / citations of data and sources | 4 |

## Code quality (15)

| Component | Points |
|---|---|
| Code runs cleanly (renders from scratch) | 5 |
| Meaningfully commented | 4 |
| Code in appendix, not body | 3 |
| Reproducible from GitHub repo | 3 |

## Reproducibility (10)

| Component | Points |
|---|---|
| GitHub repo well-organized with README | 4 |
| All team members have commits | 3 |
| Data accessible (in repo or via working URL) | 3 |

## Video presentation (10)

| Component | Points |
|---|---|
| Within time limit (5–7 min) | 2 |
| Each team member speaks | 3 |
| Covers question, data, key findings | 3 |
| Coherent, well-paced, audible | 2 |

## AI use & integrity (5)

| Component | Points |
|---|---|
| AI use note included in report | 2 |
| Honest attribution of external sources | 3 |

**Total: 100**

# Individual adjustments

Project grades may be adjusted up or down by up to 10 points per individual based on the oral checkpoints and observable team contribution. A student who could not engage with the project at the oral checkpoints will receive a lower individual grade than their team's collective work would suggest.

# Late policy

Late work for the final project requires a request to the instructor **at least 24 hours before the deadline**, with evidence of progress and a proposed new deadline. Without prior arrangement, late final reports lose 10 points per 24 hours.
